name: Felling axe
description: A long two-handed axe with a hickory haft and a broad steel head, made for felling trees and splitting logs.
notes: Lies flat along x with the head at +x and the edge on +z, gripped near the knob. The box is the T shape: mostly air round the haft and head. chopping follows the fire axe in the catalogue. Melee stats are left for tuning: a slow, heavy cutting swing.

name: Bronze axe
description: A long-hafted axe with a cast bronze head, heavier to swing than it is sharp.
notes: Rides on the felling axe's model with a bronze head. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy; chopping one step below steel.

name: Copper hatchet
description: A short stick with a wedge of copper set through a split in its head and bound tight with rawhide.
notes: Lies flat with the wedge on +z. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy.

name: Stone axe head
description: A ground stone wedge with one sharpened edge, ready to bind onto a haft or to chop with in the hand.
notes: A celt 150 mm long, 75 mm across the edge, lying flat with the edge on +z. The taper leaves part of the box empty. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy.

name: Metal axe head
description: A wedge of scrap steel ground to an edge, ready to bind onto a haft.
notes: Rides on the stone axe head's model in rusted steel. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy.

name: Hatchet
description: A one-handed axe with a square hammer poll, as handy for driving stakes as for splitting kindling.
notes: Lies flat with the head at +x and the edge on +z. The T shape leaves part of the box empty. Fine hammering folds into hammering; butchering is not carried over.

name: Crash axe
description: A short rescue axe with an insulated grip, carried aboard aircraft to cut through panels and pry open hatches.
notes: Rides on the hatchet's model with a black grip and a yellow-painted head; a real crash axe has a pick poll and a sawback, which would want its own row. prying is reasoned from its rescue use.

name: Stone adze
description: A bent stick with a stone blade lashed across its foot, swung like a hoe to shave and hollow wood.
notes: Lies flat: the stick along x, a short foot bent toward +z at its head and the blade lashed on the foot's front with its edge across the swing, so the blade stands 52 mm tall. The L shape leaves much of the box empty. Rough sawing maps to planing 1, for dressing wood; butchering is not carried over. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy.

name: Stone axe
description: A stout stick with a ground stone head set through it and bound above and below with rawhide.
notes: Lies flat with the head at +x and the edge on +z. The T shape leaves part of the box empty. A crafted item, so it has no loot economy; butchering is not carried over.

name: Bow saw
description: A thin blade strung tight across a bent steel tube, quick work for branches and firewood.
notes: Lies flat: the blade along x with its teeth on -z and the red bow arching over +z, a black grip on the rear end and a tension lever at the front. The open bow leaves much of the box empty. No axe quality or butchering is carried over: a saw does not chop.

name: Chainsaw
description: A petrol chainsaw with a long bar, for felling and bucking trees, and a brutal weapon once started.
notes: Stands on its base with the bar to +x: orange powerhead, pull starter and fuel cap on -z, closed rear handle, wrap handle and chain brake guard over the top. The model takes a real 18 inch saw's size. sawing 3 ranks it above hand saws. Fuel, starting it and its running melee use have no fields in this draft. The size is a placeholder.

name: Pole saw
description: A small petrol chainsaw head on a long shaft, for cutting branches overhead from the ground.
notes: Rides on the chainsaw's model; a pole saw's 2 m shaft with a small head at its end is a different shape that wants its own row. Fuel and starting it have no fields in this draft.

name: Cordless circular saw
description: A battery circular saw with a 165 mm blade under a sprung guard, for straight cuts through boards and sheet.
notes: Stands on its aluminium shoe, blade on +z under a fixed guard with a red lower guard, motor on -z, closed handle on top and the battery at the back. The model takes a real saw's size around a 165 mm blade and motor. sawing follows the other powered saws in the catalogue. Battery charge and its melee use have no fields. The size is a placeholder.

name: Battery chainsaw
description: A green battery chainsaw, quieter than a petrol saw and as quick to bite into wood or anything else.
notes: Shares the chainsaw's layout with a green body, a battery pack in the top and no starter. As for the petrol chainsaw, the model takes a real 18 inch saw's size. Battery charge and its running melee use have no fields. The size is a placeholder.

name: Corded electric chainsaw
description: An electric chainsaw that runs off mains power through a long cord.
notes: Rides on the battery chainsaw's model; the battery slot is drawn in the body colour as a cord housing. Mains power has no field in this draft.

name: Wood saw
description: A taper-bladed hand saw in a closed wooden handle, for cutting logs into planks and boards to length.
notes: Lies flat in the xz plane with the teeth on -z, as the hand saw does. sawing 2 sits above Deadvox's panel hand saw; no axe quality or butchering is carried over.
